---
title: "Batch correction before fitting"
description: "Remove cell-state-specific batch shifts from simulated expression with correct_feature_batch(), then fit EBMF."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

A batch shift that differs between cell states cannot be removed by centering
each batch once. `correct_feature_batch()` fits Harmony's ridge regression on
batch within each cluster of similar samples and subtracts the batch terms
from the feature matrix. This article plants such shifts in simulated data and
fits EBMF with and without the correction.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3)
have_harmony <- requireNamespace("harmony", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r simulate}
library(flashier.utils)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(5)

# two cell states with one program each, three batches crossed with state
n <- 90
state <- rep(c("alpha", "beta"), each = n / 2)
batch <- rep(c("b1", "b2", "b3"), length.out = n)
activity_truth <- cbind(alpha = (state == "alpha") * 2, beta = (state == "beta") * 2) +
  matrix(runif(2 * n, 0, 0.3), n, 2)
effect_truth <- cbind(alpha = c(rep(1.5, 5), rep(0, 7)), beta = c(rep(0, 5), rep(1.5, 5), 0, 0))
truth <- tcrossprod(activity_truth, effect_truth)

# batch b2 raises genes 1-3 in beta samples only; b3 raises genes 6-8 in alpha samples only
shift <- outer(batch == "b2" & state == "beta", c(1, 1, 1, rep(0, 9))) +
  outer(batch == "b3" & state == "alpha", c(rep(0, 5), 1, 1, 1, rep(0, 4)))
X <- truth + 1.2 * shift + matrix(rnorm(n * 12, sd = 0.15), n, 12)
dimnames(X) <- list(sprintf("s%02d", seq_len(n)), sprintf("g%02d", 1:12))
metadata <- data.frame(sample = rownames(X), batch = batch, state = state)
```

The shifts are confounded with neither state nor batch alone: batch b2 moves
genes 1 to 3 only in beta samples, and batch b3 moves genes 6 to 8 only in
alpha samples.

## Correct, then fit

Here the cluster labels are the simulated states. On real data they come from
clustering, or from soft assignments made by `harmony_assignments()` (last
section).

```{r correct}
corrected <- correct_feature_batch(X, "rows", metadata, "batch", assignments = "state")

fit_settings <- list(
  max_factors = 4, var_type = 2L, backfit = TRUE, nullcheck = TRUE, seed = 1, verbose = 0,
  ebnm_fn = list(ebnm::ebnm_point_exponential, ebnm::ebnm_point_laplace),
  feature_scale = "simulated_intensity"
)
fit_raw <- do.call(fit_ebmf, c(list(X, "rows"), fit_settings))
fit_corrected <- do.call(fit_ebmf, c(list(corrected, "rows"), fit_settings))
view_raw <- standardize_factors(fit_raw)
view_corrected <- standardize_factors(fit_corrected)
```

## Does a factor still follow batch?

For each factor, the share of its activity variance explained by batch within
state, from a linear model `activity ~ state + batch` against `activity ~ state`.

```{r batch-share}
batch_share <- function(view, label) {
  activity <- view$activity[metadata$sample, , drop = FALSE]
  shares <- apply(activity, 2, function(a) {
    rss_state <- sum(resid(lm(a ~ state))^2)
    rss_both <- sum(resid(lm(a ~ state + batch))^2)
    if (rss_state == 0) 0 else 1 - rss_both / rss_state
  })
  data.frame(input = label, factor = names(shares), batch_share = unname(shares))
}
shares <- rbind(batch_share(view_raw, "uncorrected"), batch_share(view_corrected, "corrected"))
shares$input <- factor(shares$input, levels = c("uncorrected", "corrected"))
shares
```

```{r batch-share-plot, fig.alt="Bar chart of the within-state batch share of activity variance for each factor, fitted on uncorrected and on corrected input.", fig.cap="Within-state batch share of each factor's activity variance. Bars start at zero; one bar per factor."}
ggplot(shares, aes(factor, batch_share)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#0072B2") +
  facet_wrap(~input, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "batch share of within-state variance") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r numbers, include=FALSE}
max_share <- tapply(shares$batch_share, shares$input, max)
n_factors <- c(uncorrected = ncol(view_raw$activity), corrected = ncol(view_corrected$activity))
```

On the uncorrected input the fit has `r n_factors[["uncorrected"]]` factors, and
the most batch-driven one has `r round(max_share[["uncorrected"]], 2)` of its
within-state variance explained by batch. After correction the fit has
`r n_factors[["corrected"]]` factors, and the largest batch share is
`r round(max_share[["corrected"]], 2)`. This is one simulated dataset with
known states, not a calibration of the method.

## Keep a covariate you want to study

If donors or conditions are nested in batch, the correction also removes their
effect within each cluster. Name such covariates in `protect`: they enter each
cluster's regression without penalty and are not subtracted.

```{r protect, eval=FALSE}
correct_feature_batch(X, "rows", metadata, "batch", "state", protect = ~condition)
```

Batch should be technical. Correcting by donor also removes the donor
differences that a later `test_factor_association()` on a donor-level
condition would test.

## Soft assignments from Harmony

```{r harmony-skip, echo=FALSE, results="asis", eval=!have_harmony}
cat("Check skipped: the harmony package is not installed.\n")
```

```{r harmony, eval=have_harmony}
pcs <- prcomp(X, rank. = 4)$x
h <- harmony_assignments(pcs, metadata, "batch", seed = 1, nclust = 4)
corrected_soft <- correct_feature_batch(X, "rows", metadata, "batch", h$assignments, lambda = h$lambda)
# within-state difference of b2 from b1 on genes 1-3, before and after
in_beta <- metadata$state == "beta"
gap <- function(Y) {
  colMeans(Y[in_beta & batch == "b2", 1:3]) - colMeans(Y[in_beta & batch == "b1", 1:3])
}
round(rbind(uncorrected = gap(X), corrected = gap(corrected_soft)), 2)
```

The automatic penalty shrinks the batch terms toward zero, so part of each
shift remains. A smaller `alpha` (passed to Harmony through
`.options = harmony::harmony_options(alpha = ...)`) gives a weaker penalty,
which should remove more of it; this article does not test that.

The corrected matrix is part of the fit. For `factor_stability()` or
`factor_holdout()`, run the correction inside the `fit_fn` callback on each
resample; correcting once beforehand overstates stability.

## Credits

The correction is Harmony's mixture-of-experts ridge step (Korsunsky et al.
2019, *Nature Methods* 16:1289-1296), applied to the feature matrix as in
Dylan Kotliar's cNMF `Preprocess`. See [CREDITS](https://github.com/mdmanurung/flashier-utils/blob/main/CREDITS.md).
